author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Dr. Brenda Lau, a pain specialist with over 25 years of experience, challenges the idea that weakness is an inevitable part of aging. After being diagnosed with osteopenia despite decades of exercise, she realized that health care overlooks the body’s core system: strength. Drawing on personal experience, research, and patient stories, she introduces three simple daily questions—Move, Lift, Protein—that rebuild strength at any age. These are not fitness trends, but biological switches that protect muscles, bones, and independence, especially for women. Dr. Lau reframes strength as freedom, urging us to stop accepting frailty as normal and to actively build resilience, mobility, and confidence throughout life. Dr. Brenda Lau is a dual-fellowship anesthesiologist, pain specialist, and hypnotherapist who has spent over 25 years helping people heal when medicine alone isn’t enough. A pioneer in Pain Medicine in Canada and the founder of Changepain — the country’s largest acc
title: How strength training helps women age healthier | Dr. Brenda Lau | TEDxSurrey

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most women experience motherhood as a professional setback with lost years and stalled momentum. Diana argues it's the exact opposite: that it is the place where leadership skills are not just created, but amplified. Drawing on her experience from motherhood into a demanding finance career, she reveals the Recognition Gap — the space between the leadership skills motherhood actually builds and the ones society has been trained to recognize. Through concrete examples of decision-making under uncertainty, emotional regulation, and long-term strategic thinking, she shows how the same capabilities are praised in corporate settings but routinely dismissed when practiced at home, and why closing that gap matters for everyone.
 Diana Dinh is a licensed financial strategist and founder of Mama Masterminds, a community bringing entrepreneurial mothers together across Greater Vancouver. She helps women protect, grow, and transfer wealth in ways that create stability for their families and futur
title: How motherhood builds better leaders | Diana Dinh | TEDxWest Vancouver Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this TEDxRUAS talk, Amrita Mukherjee explores why Emotional Intelligence remains the true differentiator in a world increasingly shaped by Artificial Intelligence. Drawing from decades of experience in global banking and technology, she reflects on how success has long been measured by IQ, even though cognitive ability explains only a fraction of real-world performance. Through examples spanning corporate boardrooms and tech teams, she highlights how brilliance without emotional awareness creates friction, while those who balance intellect with empathy build trust, collaboration and lasting impact. As AI takes over logic, design and even conversation, she presents a paradox—we are surrounded by answers, yet lacking understanding. While AI can process data with precision, it cannot perceive emotion, interpret silence or offer genuine compassion. Through her journey from corporate leadership to founding a women’s coaching platform, she shows how AI can be a powerful tool, but Emotion
title: The Constant in a World of Change: Why EI Will Outlast AI  | Ms Amrita Mukherjee | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this TEDxRUAS talk, Dr. Priyanka Reddy redefines what it truly means to heal, challenging the idea that medicine is limited to diagnoses, reports, and prescriptions. Through powerful patient stories, she brings to light a deeper truth that healing goes beyond treating disease, and lies in understanding the person behind it, their fears, lifestyle, and emotional struggles. She introduces the concept of a “second degree” for modern doctors, built on empathy, the mindful use of technology, and strong leadership. More than a perspective on medicine, this talk is a reminder that while healthcare continues to evolve, its essence remains rooted in compassion, connection, and care. Dr. Priyanka Reddy is a  board-certified dermatologist & trichologist with advanced aesthetic training from the USA, she blends clinical science with a holistic, patient-first approach. With a total digital community of over 2.1 million, she is one of India’s leading voices in evidence-based skincare and modern
title: The Paradox of Healing | Dr Priyanka Reddy | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDxRUAS talk, Syed Kirmani reflects on a life shaped by discipline, perseverance, and teamwork through the lens of “Timeless Flux” - the balance between changing circumstances and enduring values. Revisiting India’s historic 1983 Cricket World Cup victory, he shares stories of pressure, preparation, and belief that transformed a team of underdogs into world champions. He also recalls how his father initially prioritized academics and encouraged him to focus on studies, but later became one of his strongest supporters after recognizing his deep passion and commitment to cricket.

Through experiences on and off the field, he speaks about resilience, humility, and the importance of staying grounded even at the height of success. Drawing from decades in international cricket, he reflects on how sport becomes a teacher of life, where setbacks build character and consistency matters more than applause. Beyond cricket, he explores leadership, mentorship, and the responsibility of in
title: Between the Wickets and Beyond | Padma Shri Syed Kirmani | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this TEDxRUAS talk, Srinivasulu IFS takes us through a powerful and introspective journey of navigating life through what he calls “Timeless Flux”: the balance between constant change and enduring values. Through moments of academic struggle, unexpected setbacks, and self-discovery, he reflects on the importance of resilience, humility, and trusting effort over outcomes. Drawing from his experiences wildlife conservation, he shares how true impact lies not just in protecting forests, but in empowering the communities around them, and how simple, human-centered ideas can create lasting change. More than a story of service, it is a story of purpose, adaptability, and finding meaning in life’s uncertainties. Srinivasulu is a distinguished IFS officer with over two decades of leadership in forestry, wildlife, and environmental governance. Renowned for blending conservation, technology, and sustainability, his tenure across key roles has driven innovation, eco-restoration, and citizen e
title: Between Change and Constancy | Mr Srinivasulu IFS | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this heartfelt TEDxRUAS talk, Samyukta Hornad reflects on a journey shaped by pain, belonging, and purpose. Using the metaphor of a dying lion, she introduces the idea of “timeless flux,” where strength and surrender coexist, reminding us that true power often lies in acceptance. She opens up about her struggles with bullying and the constant need for validation, revealing how even success in acting could not fill her inner emptiness.

A turning point in her life came through the unconditional love of her dog, Gunda, which led her toward healing and compassion. This transformation inspired her to found the Praana Animal Foundation, through which she has rescued thousands of animals and built a more compassionate ecosystem for all living beings. Samyukta Hornad is a celebrated Indian actress, social entrepreneur, and animal welfare advocate based in Bengaluru. With over 34 films and web series across South Indian cinema, she has earned accolades including the Filmfare Award and SIIM
title: Somewhere I Belong | Ms Samyukta Hornad | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDxRUAS talk, Praveen Kamath Kumbla takes the audience through a deeply personal journey across the intersections of technology, education, creativity, and human connection. Through the lens of “Timeless Flux,” he reflects on how continuous learning, adaptability, and meaningful relationships shape both personal and professional growth. From becoming an All India Radio artist at the age of thirteen to building networks across art, sports, business, and education, he shares how passion and curiosity opened doors to unexpected opportunities. 

Drawing from decades of experience as an educator and mentor, he explores the importance of embracing change with purpose rather than fear. He speaks about how classrooms became spaces of transformation, where technology and human values could coexist to create lasting impact. Beyond professional success, he reflects on his evolution from a career-driven mindset to one rooted in wisdom, contribution, and inner fulfillment. Praveen Kamath
title: Humans, Technology, and Life  | Dr Praveen Kamath K | TEDxRUAS

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Am I still the same person when I speak different languages—or do different versions of me emerge? This talk explores how language shapes identity, emotion, and the way we present ourselves to the world. It invites us to question whether our sense of self is fixed, or fluid across the languages we speak. I am a 17 year old student from Russia. Snowboarding is my passion, and I love reading detective novels.

My talk will be about identity and language. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Am I Not the Same Person in every Language? | Kira Monakhova | TEDxBBIS Youth

This talk explores how listening, reflection, and thoughtful communication can be powerful tools for leadership and connection. It challenges the idea that you have to be the loudest to make an impact. I am a 14 year old Indian student currently studying in Hungary. I am particularly interested in researching social topics. Dans ce TEDx, Martin Fouillé explore les croyances, les peurs et les conditionnements qui façonnent notre rapport à l’argent. 
Cette conférence invite chacun à questionner la place qu’il donne à l’argent dans ses choix et ses projets.
L’objectif : remettre l’argent au service de votre vie. 
Une invitation à reprendre le pouvoir sur sa relation à l’argent, pour construire une vie plus alignée et consciente. Martin Fouillé accompagne, depuis l’âge de 18 ans, professionnels et particuliers pour les aider à mettre leur argent au service de leurs projets de vie.

Conseiller en gestion de patrimoine de père en fils, il a grandi au contact de ces sujets qui influencent profondément nos choix, nos peurs et nos ambitions.

Très tôt, il se passionne pour la relation intime — et souvent conflictuelle — que chacun entretient avec l’argent. Un sujet central dans nos vies, mais paradoxalement tenu à distance : tabou, s

description:
Bazen bir karar, bir adımla başlar.Ve o adım, bir dönüşüme dönüşür.

Bugün düzenlediği etkinliklerle yüzlerce insanı bir araya getiren Naz Karagözoğlu, sporun şehirle ve insanlarla kurduğu bağı yeniden tanımlıyor. 19 yaşında, hayatındaki en sevdiği insanın hastalık haberini aldığı gün basketbol ayakkabılarını giyip koşuya çıkmış; o gün koşunun zihinsel iyileşme alanı olduğunu keşfetmiştir. Bu farkındalıkla Alsancak Runners topluluğunu kurmuştur.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk presents mindfulness through a more direct and grounded lens, shaped by personal loss, identity shifts, and psychological insight. Dr. Shambhavi Samar begins by questioning a common assumption. Unity is often treated as something external, yet the real conflict lies within the self.
Drawing from her recent experience with endometrial cancer and the emotional impact of losing organs tied to identity, she examines what remains when familiar definitions fall away. In that space, she introduces the idea of “Kali” not as a symbol of destruction, but as a form of clear awareness that cuts through illusion.
The talk connects this inner process to broader social dynamics. When individuals fail to understand their own emotional complexity, they struggle to accept differences in others. True unity, she argues, depends on the ability to sit with discomfort, contradiction, and change.
At the centre of the talk is a practical framework. The K.A.L.I formula, which stands for Know, Accept,
title: Awaken the Kali Within: A Mindfulness Equation | Dr. Shambhavi Samar | TEDxGGSIPU

description: Explore how pursuing your passion can transform your life from comfortable but empty to risky yet meaningful. Aashna shares lessons on choosing courage over comfort and the growth that only happens when we step into discomfort. Aashna is a driven and passionate Grade 8 student who enjoys reading, listening to music, and traveling. She has a strong love for sports, especially horse riding, basketball, badminton, and tennis. Through her talk, Aashna highlights how pursuing one’s passions adds meaning and fulfillment to life, and she hopes to inspire others to follow their inner flame. She is also the co-founder of ElevatEd Indonesia and is known as a public speaker and content creator who shares insights on student life, self development, and youth empowerment. description: Aulia Azza invites the audience to look beyond the relentless, fast-paced rhythm of the global fashion industry to see the hidden environmental costs right here in Indonesia. This talk challenges us to confront our responsibilities as consumers, showing how mindful consumption can transform our everyday wardrobes into a powerful narrative of change, proving that our choices are ultimately our most valuable works of art. Aulia Azza is a storyteller at heart, currently shaping narratives as a Reporter at HighEnd Magazine while pursuing her degree in Digital Communication and Media at IPB University. She has built a diverse professional portfolio spanning fashion journalism, branding, and public relations. Aulia is known for her advocacy of mindful consumption and sustainability values, she uses her platform to inspire others and demonstrate how au
title: The Artful Undercurrent of Fashion | Aulia Azza | TEDxIPB

author: TEDx Talks
description: Astrophysicist Milad Delfan Azari traces the journey of the atoms inside us — forged in the violent hearts of dying stars and scattered across the universe — reminding us that we are not separate from the cosmos, but literally made of it.  Milad Delfan Azari is an Assistant Professor at Temple University Japan whose research spans neutrino astrophysics and high-energy astrophysical objects. He earned his Ph.D. in Physics from Waseda University in Tokyo, where he subsequently held a postdoctoral research position. A member of both The Physical Society of Japan and The Astronomical Society of Japan, Milad brings rare clarity to some of the biggest questions in modern physics — translating the language of supernovae and nuclear fusion into something immediate, human, and deeply personal. His work reminds us that astrophysics is not just the study of distant objects, but the story of where we all come from. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independen
title: From exploding starts to human life | Milad Delfan Azari | TEDxTUJ

description: Social media influencer Kyle Metcalf makes a counterintuitive case: embarrassment isn't something to avoid — it's a sign that growth is already underway. Through personal stories of stumbling through Japanese conversations and deliberately stepping into uncomfortable situations, Kyle challenges us to rethink failure and recognize that real progress begins the moment we're willing to look foolish. Kyle Metcalf is an American creator living in Japan who is documenting his journey to Japanese fluency by striking up conversations with strangers across the country. What began as a personal language-learning experiment has grown into a global audience of millions, drawn to his honest and often hilarious accounts of navigating life across cultural and linguistic boundaries. title: Mistakes are the price we pay for growth | Kyle Metcalf | TEDxTUJ

description: Javaid Sharoon shares the story of walking from Tokyo to Kyoto, using the journey to explore a simple idea that it is not the sole that carries you but the soul, the resilience, mindset, and inner strength that truly move you forward. Sharoon is part of the Social Media Team at Temple University Japan Campus, where he creates content that captures student life and connects communities across cultures. His experiences adjusting to life in Japan — and the unexpected lessons those struggles taught him — form the foundation of his TEDx talk.

 Christian Collazo is a postgraduate student in the Communications Managment program at Temple University Japan, Kyoto Campus. Originally fromthe U.S., he came to Japan and navigated the challenges of building a new life across cultural and linguistic boundaries. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: Mezzo-soprano Ayaka Tanimoto takes the stage with a spellbinding rendition of "L'amour est un oiseau rebelle," the iconic Habanera from Georges Bizet's Carmen (1875). With commanding stage presence and deep emotional resonance, Ayaka reminds us why this aria has captivated audiences for 150 years.  Originally from Japan, Ayaka relocated to London and subsequently graduated from Royal College of Music with a Bachelor of Music (BMus Hons) and a Masters in Vocal Performance (MPerf). Additionally, Ayaka graduated as a Scholar from the Royal Conservatoire of Scotland Alexander Gibson Opera School. Ayaka has won numerous awards in Japan and UK and she has taken to the stage as a recitalist in a number of highly regarded venues throughout UK such as the Purcell Room, National Gallery, King’s Place, St. Martin in the Fields, St. James’ Piccadilly, Portsmouth Cathedral, and Bristol Cathedral to name but a few. She has sung with opera companies such as English National Opera, Longborough Opera

description:
Vikram Kochar shares an honest and inspiring journey of embracing failure and constantly reinventing himself as an actor. From struggling academically and failing in physics in Class 12 to discovering theatre through extracurricular admissions at Kirori Mal College, he reflects on how unexpected setbacks opened new doors in life.
Through stories of theatre, training at the National School of Drama, and years of relentless auditions in Mumbai, Kochar highlights the importance of learning, unlearning, and persistence. His journey from a “free actor” doing unpaid work to building a career across films, series, ads, and theatre shows that success often comes from resilience and patience.
Ultimately, his message is simple yet powerful: life has no fixed path, failure can be a great teacher, and the goal is not to prove yourself to others but to keep improving every day. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sudhir Mishra reflects on the evolution of human learning and how the development of society gradually shaped structured systems of education and thinking. Over time, standardized methods of teaching uniform syllabi, examinations, and routines helped societies function efficiently, but they also conditioned individuals to think within fixed frameworks.
He explains that while learning new knowledge is relatively easy, the real challenge lies in unlearning deeply held beliefs and assumptions. Drawing on examples from science, he highlights how shifting from classical Newtonian physics to modern quantum concepts requires not only learning new ideas but also letting go of earlier mental models. This process illustrates why unlearning is often the most difficult step in intellectual growth.
Through his experience working on the development of the BrahMos missile system, he demonstrates how teams of scientists repeatedly had to relearn and redesign technologies for different environments—se
title: The Hardest Lesson in Science: How to Unlearn What You Know | Sudhir Kumar Mishra | TEDxIIMRohtak

description:
Shivam Khajuria shares his journey of navigating uncertainty, career confusion, and unexpected opportunities while building a life in the entertainment industry. From studying engineering without passion to discovering comfort in front of the camera through modelling, he reflects on how embracing change helped him find direction.
Through stories of working corporate jobs, surviving Mumbai during COVID as a call centre executive, and relentlessly auditioning through self-tests, Shivam highlights how persistence and adaptability shaped his acting career.
He explains how success in any field requires a continuous cycle of learning, unlearning, and relearning, letting go of limiting beliefs, staying grounded through success, and constantly evolving with changing times. Ultimately, his message is that growth never stops, and writing your own life’s script means showing up every day ready to learn again.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dr. Satyapal reflects on a lifetime of public service from his years in the Indian Police Service to his role in public life through the lens of learning, unlearning, and relearning. Drawing from leadership experiences in policing and governance, he highlights how continuous learning builds wisdom and humility.
He explains that true growth requires the courage to unlearn outdated beliefs, step out of comfort zones, and question long-held assumptions. His transition from police leadership to public life taught him the importance of dialogue, empathy, and adaptability.
Ultimately, he emphasizes that in a rapidly changing world, the ability to learn, unlearn, and relearn is the most essential leadership skill. By staying curious, grounded in values, and open to change, individuals can remain relevant, purposeful, and prepared to lead in an evolving society.

description:
Preeti Dimri shares an inspiring journey that began with her mother’s dream of seeing one of her children become a cricketer. From a four-year-old girl in Agra playing with borrowed equipment and facing physical struggles, she reflects on how determination and her mother’s unwavering belief shaped her path in cricket.
Through powerful stories of travelling alone for trials, playing senior nationals at just 12, and eventually wearing the India jersey, she highlights the grit required to succeed in competitive sports.
She also speaks about the difficult phase after injuries and selection setbacks, and how she rebuilt her identity beyond playing through commentary and contributing to cricket off the field. Ultimately, her message celebrates resilience, gratitude, and the power of dreams born in small towns.

description:
Pratishtha Deveshwar shares a deeply personal journey of resilience after a life-changing accident at the age of thirteen left her paralysed from the waist down. Waking up in an ICU and hearing the words “you will never walk again” felt like the end of her world. In that moment, life forced her into the most difficult lesson she would ever learn, learning, unlearning, and relearning how to live.
She explains how the first step was learning to see possibilities instead of loss. Looking at herself in a wheelchair, she realized that although she had lost movement, she still had her mind, ambition, and voice to rebuild her life. The next step was unlearning the limitations placed on her by society. People constantly told her what she could not do, but she refused to accept that narrative and chose independence, education, and self-belief instead.

title: If You Can't Walk… Fly: Rising Beyond Life's Limits | Pratishtha Deveshwar | TEDxIIMRohtak

description:
Prafful Garg reflects on his journey from a lower-middle-class upbringing in Agra to becoming a journalist, entrepreneur, and digital creator reaching millions. Through personal experiences from building platforms without resources to navigating career-defining choices he explores how growth comes through continuous learning.
He explains that true transformation requires not only gaining knowledge but also unlearning limiting beliefs about success, background, and comfort. By letting go of fear, comparison, and rigid career paths, individuals can create space for new opportunities and authentic growth.
Ultimately, he emphasizes that thriving in a rapidly changing world requires a lifelong cycle of learning, unlearning, and relearning. Success is not defined by circumstances but by the courage to evolve, adapt, and constantly rewrite your own path.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Gurmangal Das reflects on how growing up in a historically vibrant village in Punjab shaped his belief that individuals have a responsibility to contribute to society. Inspired by stories of freedom fighters and community leaders he learned about in school, he began questioning why those who benefited from their sacrifices should not also work toward building a better society.
His idea of success followed a conventional path studying engineering, going abroad, earning money, and sending it back to support his village. However, witnessing the social challenges faced by youth in Punjab, including the effects of militancy, the absence of role models, and rising issues such as drug abuse and academic failure, forced him to rethink this definition of success.
Through a process of learning, unlearning, and relearning, he realized that meaningful change required being present within the community rather than supporting it from afar. This insight led to the creation of the Youth Football Club
title: Play It Forward: How Sports Can Rebuild a Village | Gurmangal Dass | TEDxIIMRohtak
